purpose: Find missing scientific capabilities and design realistic, executable Harbor workflows. Skills and biological applications are independent facets; they are not a hierarchy or a Cartesian task-generation grid.

skills.name: Normalization
skills.outcome: Adjust measurement scale or composition using a declared normalization procedure.
skills.include: Rescale counts, library sizes or measurement distributions as a required operation.
skills.exclude: Reading normalized inputs; logarithms alone; normalization internal to a method without a separate required result.

skills.name: Data transformation
skills.outcome: Apply a defined mathematical transformation while preserving identities, missingness and units.
skills.include: Apply an explicitly requested mathematical change of variables.
skills.exclude: Already transformed inputs; generic format conversion; incidental transformations internal to another skill.

skills.name: Dimensionality reduction
skills.outcome: Construct a reduced representation and check its fit, variance or neighborhood properties.
skills.include: Compute or assess a low-dimensional representation or its variance.
skills.exclude: Using a supplied embedding; merely drawing coordinates; interpreting a plot without computing an embedding.

skills.name: Feature selection
skills.outcome: Select informative features under a declared criterion without leaking evaluation data.

skills.name: Association analysis
skills.outcome: Estimate or test an association on correctly matched observations with the stated unit of replication.
skills.include: Estimate dependence or test an association between matched variables.
skills.exclude: A benchmark grader using correlation; retrieving an association record; claiming causation.

skills.name: Regression modeling
skills.outcome: Fit a specified response model and report parameters, uncertainty or fit diagnostics.
skills.include: Estimate response-model parameters, uncertainty, contrasts or fit diagnostics.
skills.exclude: Prediction-only submissions; regression used internally for differential expression without a separate model-analysis endpoint.

skills.name: Group comparison
skills.outcome: Estimate or test a group contrast with explicit sampling, pairing and effect direction.
skills.include: Compare groups with an explicit contrast, unit of replication and test or effect estimate.
skills.exclude: Every specialized differential expression or abundance task; a supplied group contrast.

skills.name: Multiple-testing correction
skills.outcome: Correct a declared family of hypothesis tests and retain its tested population.
skills.include: Choose, apply or audit a multiple-testing procedure as an explicit analysis requirement.
skills.exclude: Counting an already thresholded gene list; an internal default adjustment with no independent requirement.

skills.name: Differential expression analysis
skills.outcome: Estimate expression contrasts under an explicit design, measurement model and gene-selection rule.
skills.include: Compute or audit gene/transcript expression contrasts and their significance or effect selection.
skills.exclude: Predicting supplied differential-expression values in unseen perturbations; looking up a published DEG list.

skills.name: Enrichment analysis
skills.outcome: Quantify gene-set, pathway or feature overrepresentation relative to a declared universe.

skills.name: Sensitivity analysis
skills.outcome: Repeat an analysis under controlled changes and quantify the resulting differences.

skills.name: Clustering
skills.outcome: Partition observations and assess grouping stability, separation or external agreement.

skills.name: Predictive classification
skills.outcome: Predict labels or probabilities for withheld observations with a prespecified metric.
skills.include: Produce discrete labels or class probabilities for new observations.
skills.exclude: Selecting a multiple-choice answer; retrieving known labels; specialized cell annotation without a separate generic classification task.

skills.name: Predictive regression
skills.outcome: Predict continuous outcomes for withheld observations under the required split and leakage policy.
skills.include: Predict continuous scalar or vector measurements for unseen observations under an explicit split policy.
skills.exclude: Fitting coefficients for inference; generating molecular geometry; spatial pattern scoring without a supervised prediction requirement.

skills.name: Model evaluation
skills.outcome: Evaluate complete predictions with a fixed metric and biological grouping or split policy.
skills.include: The solver computes or compares predictive performance, calibration or generalization results.
skills.exclude: The benchmark grader computes a score on submitted predictions; merely supplying test predictions or out-of-fold predictions.

skills.name: Survival analysis
skills.outcome: Estimate time-to-event quantities using explicit censoring, risk sets and covariates.

skills.name: Causal inference
skills.outcome: Estimate a specified causal contrast under explicit identification and sensitivity assumptions.

skills.name: Sequence alignment
skills.outcome: Align sequences or reads and interpret correspondence, scores and coordinate conventions.

skills.name: Sequence and annotation analysis
skills.outcome: Extract or reconcile sequences with strand, coordinate, translation and annotation rules.
skills.include: Compute sequence properties or derive sequence, translation or annotation results under explicit reference conventions.
skills.exclude: A sequence is merely an input to an unrelated operation; parsing a FASTA as an incidental step.

skills.name: Genomic interval analysis
skills.outcome: Compute coordinate-aware overlap, distance, coverage or interval transformations.
skills.include: Compute genomic overlaps, distances, windows or interval mappings.
skills.exclude: A database lookup whose query mentions a promoter; intervals already resolved in the input.

skills.name: Sequencing quality and coverage analysis
skills.outcome: Measure read, alignment and reference coverage with explicit eligibility and denominators.

skills.name: Sequence assembly and assessment
skills.outcome: Assemble or assess contigs using observed read support, continuity and error evidence.

skills.name: Variant analysis
skills.outcome: Call, normalize, filter or summarize variants with explicit allele and sample semantics.

skills.name: Variant consequence annotation
skills.outcome: Connect alleles to transcript, protein or regulatory consequences under pinned references.
skills.include: Derive transcript, protein or regulatory consequences of alleles against reference annotations.
skills.exclude: Retrieving an existing ClinVar assertion; predicting protein assay fitness; generic mention of pathogenicity.

skills.name: Population genetic analysis
skills.outcome: Estimate allele-frequency, ancestry, differentiation or inheritance quantities.

skills.name: Orthology assessment
skills.outcome: Assess homologous gene identity, completeness and copy status across proteomes.

skills.name: Phylogenetic inference and tree analysis
skills.outcome: Infer or measure trees with explicit topology, branch-length, rooting and taxon conventions.
skills.include: Infer a phylogeny or calculate an explicitly requested tree property.
skills.exclude: Lineage mentioned as biological context; a clustering dendrogram with no evolutionary interpretation.

skills.name: Alignment informativeness and composition
skills.outcome: Measure informative sites and sequence composition under explicit gap and residue rules.

skills.name: Cell identity annotation
skills.outcome: Assign or compare cell identities against declared reference evidence and an abstention policy.
skills.include: Assign or audit cell identity from expression, markers or labeled reference cells.
skills.exclude: Receiving cell types as metadata; interpreting changes within already annotated cell types.

skills.name: Population composition analysis
skills.outcome: Compare population counts and fractions while preserving sample-level denominators and replication.

skills.name: Data integration
skills.outcome: Reconcile batches, studies or modalities and evaluate alignment without erasing the target variation.
skills.include: Align or reconcile batches/modalities and assess their correspondence.
skills.exclude: Predicting one modality from another; using pre-aligned tables or supplied integrated embeddings.

skills.name: Mixture deconvolution
skills.outcome: Estimate component abundances or signals using declared references and identifiable mixtures.

skills.name: Trajectory and dynamics analysis
skills.outcome: Estimate ordered states or dynamics and distinguish model-derived order from measured time.

skills.name: Cell communication analysis
skills.outcome: Compute expression-supported ligand–receptor or sender–receiver evidence under a frozen reference.

skills.name: Spatial analysis
skills.outcome: Quantify spatial relationships, neighborhoods or gradients with explicit geometry and null models.

skills.name: Chromatin accessibility and binding analysis
skills.outcome: Analyze accessibility or binding signals using controls, replicates and reference-aware regions.
skills.include: Compute or interpret accessibility, chromatin occupancy or contact signals.
skills.exclude: DNA substrings spelling ATAC; general gene regulation; retrieving a stored binding-site assertion.

skills.name: Motif analysis
skills.outcome: Find or assess sequence motifs under explicit models and background composition.

skills.name: Methylation analysis
skills.outcome: Quantify methylation at sites or regions with coverage, measurement-unit and reference rules.

skills.name: Network analysis
skills.outcome: Construct or evaluate typed networks, modules, paths or connectivity with traceable edges.
skills.include: Infer edges or compute modules, paths, centrality or other relational structure.
skills.exclude: Looking up one stored edge; independent pair classification with supplied features and no graph operation.

skills.name: Molecular structure analysis
skills.outcome: Measure structural geometry, residue/atom identity, contacts or structural agreement.
skills.include: Measure or compare existing three-dimensional structures, contacts or geometry.
skills.exclude: A genomic binding site; sequence-only protein work; producing new poses, which is structure prediction.

skills.name: Molecular representation and descriptors
skills.outcome: Parse chemical structures and compute graph, charge, stereochemical or descriptor properties.

skills.name: RNA structure analysis
skills.outcome: Predict or compare RNA structure under declared thermodynamic or measured constraints.

skills.name: Image measurement and reconstruction
skills.outcome: Measure or reconstruct image content with explicit calibration, pixel geometry and sample identity.
skills.include: Measure, reconstruct or process actual image pixels and geometry.
skills.exclude: Supplied image-derived tables; scientific plots; genomic segmentation; classification with no separate image-processing output.

skills.name: Signal and time-series analysis
skills.outcome: Process recorded signals or time series with explicit sampling, filtering and temporal splits.

skills.name: Dose–response and assay analysis
skills.outcome: Estimate assay responses and control-adjusted effects with declared plate, dose and replicate structure.

skills.name: Differential abundance analysis
skills.outcome: Estimate abundance contrasts under measurement, missingness and replicate conventions.

skills.name: Immune repertoire analysis
skills.outcome: Reconcile receptor chains and quantify clonotypes, diversity or sharing across samples.

skills.name: Biological database querying
skills.outcome: Resolve identifiers and retrieve versioned records under explicit query and evidence rules.
skills.include: Resolve identities and retrieve or reconcile records from a database snapshot.
skills.exclude: A database is merely the origin of already supplied data; biological inference performed by a predictive model.

skills.name: Structured evidence extraction
skills.outcome: Extract specified facts or measurements with source locations, units and a finite evidence scope.
skills.include: Extract an explicit fact or measurement with a supporting source location.
skills.exclude: A citation in background; unconstrained literature synthesis; simple structured database retrieval already covered by database querying.

skills.name: Evidence-based prioritization
skills.outcome: Rank candidates under declared evidence, eligibility and tie rules without asserting unmeasured causality.
skills.include: Prioritize candidates by an explicit, scientifically justified evidence rule.
skills.exclude: The phrase most likely in an exact database query; a surrogate rule presented as proof of causality.

skills.name: Mechanistic modeling and simulation
skills.outcome: Construct and execute a model and evaluate predictions under specified conditions and numerical rules.

skills.name: Sequence construct analysis and design
skills.outcome: Construct or audit sequence products against explicit compatibility, translation and assembly constraints.

skills.name: Statistical estimation
skills.outcome: Calculate an endpoint with correct observation units, aggregation, uncertainty and denominators.
skills.include: Estimate a standalone descriptive quantity or its uncertainty with explicit units and denominators.
skills.exclude: A mean, count or ratio that is internal to a separately labeled specialized analysis.

skills.name: Data preparation and reconciliation
skills.outcome: Join, filter, reshape or reconcile scientific records while preserving identity and provenance.
skills.include: Reconcile identities, missingness, schemas or joins as an explicit analytical deliverable.
skills.exclude: Routine file loading, incidental filtering, or saving results.

skills.name: Scientific visualization
skills.outcome: Produce a specified scientific view with checkable data, labels, scales and graphical elements.
skills.include: Create a required figure with checkable plotted data, scales and labels.
skills.exclude: Input images; a grader inspecting a plot; optional diagnostic figures.

skills.name: Taxonomic profiling
skills.outcome: Assign sequence evidence to taxa and quantify their abundance under a pinned reference and ambiguity policy.

skills.name: Expression quantification
skills.outcome: Estimate transcript or gene abundance from reads with explicit reference, multimapping and normalization rules.

skills.name: Cell and feature quality control
skills.outcome: Select cells or features using declared measurement-aware quality, contamination and doublet rules.

skills.name: Model inspection
skills.outcome: Inspect architecture, parameter identity or uncertainty from an executable model and pinned checkpoint.

skills.name: Computational experiment design
skills.outcome: Select informative perturbations or queries to distinguish models within a fixed experimental budget.
skills.include: Choose observations or simulated experiments and submit the resulting design or model.
skills.exclude: Wet-lab execution; an unrestricted research plan judged for novelty or quality.

skills.name: Image segmentation
skills.outcome: Assign pixel or voxel masks to structures under a specified label and geometry convention.
skills.include: Produce or audit segmentation masks from images.
skills.exclude: A supplied segmentation; genomic segmentation; image-level classification.

skills.name: Image object detection
skills.outcome: Localize and label objects using boxes, points or equivalent spatial annotations.
skills.include: Produce labeled object locations and confidence scores from images.
skills.exclude: Image-level labels only; masks belong to image segmentation.

skills.name: Molecular structure prediction
skills.outcome: Generate molecular conformations or binding poses with valid atom identity and geometry.
skills.include: Predict new three-dimensional coordinates or poses.
skills.exclude: Measure supplied structures; scalar affinity prediction; RNA secondary-structure inference already covered by RNA structure analysis.

skills.name: Chemical structure recognition
skills.outcome: Convert a chemical drawing to a machine-readable molecular structure.
skills.include: Recover molecular identity, connectivity and stereochemistry from a drawing.
skills.exclude: Calculate descriptors from a supplied SMILES; general image segmentation.

applications.name: Transcriptomics
applications.scope: Gene or transcript expression, abundance and expression-derived cell states. RNA biochemical stability alone is RNA biochemistry.

applications.name: Genomic variation
applications.scope: Genetic alleles, genotypes, inheritance, genetic risk and variant evidence.

applications.name: Genome and sequence analysis
applications.scope: Nucleotide sequence content, annotation, assembly and construct identity.

applications.name: Epigenomics
applications.scope: Chromatin accessibility, occupancy, contacts or DNA methylation. Gene regulation also occurs in other applications.

applications.name: Proteomics
applications.scope: Proteome-scale abundance, modification or interaction measurements. A single protein sequence or structure does not establish proteomics.

applications.name: Metabolomics
applications.scope: Metabolite identities and abundance measurements across samples.

applications.name: Molecular evolution
applications.scope: Evolutionary relationships, molecular conservation and divergence.

applications.name: Molecular structure
applications.scope: Three-dimensional biomolecular geometry, complexes and structural interactions.

applications.name: Chemical biology
applications.scope: Chemical entities, compound activity, affinity and chemical perturbation assays.

applications.name: Functional genomics
applications.scope: Gene function, regulatory relationships, pathways and gene perturbation responses.

applications.name: Microbiology
applications.scope: Microorganisms and microbial communities as the biological objects of analysis.

applications.name: Ecology
applications.scope: Populations, communities, habitats and environmental relationships.

applications.name: Clinical and epidemiological analysis
applications.scope: Patient-level outcomes, diagnosis, prognosis and epidemiological measurements. A drug-discovery motivation alone does not qualify.

applications.name: Immunology
applications.scope: Immune cells, receptors and responses as the target of the scientific question.

applications.name: Biological imaging
applications.scope: Biological or medical images and image-derived phenotype measurements. Chemical drawings and plots alone do not qualify.

applications.name: Physiology
applications.scope: Organism, organ or cell physiological function, including recorded physiological signals.

applications.name: Systems biology
applications.scope: Mechanistic system behavior, kinetics and interactions modeled at the system level. The word system alone is insufficient.

applications.name: Protein function and biochemistry
applications.scope: Protein sequence-to-function relationships and biochemical activities, including mutational scanning assays.

applications.name: RNA processing and biochemistry
applications.scope: RNA sequence-dependent processing, translation, stability and biochemical reactivity.

annotation_policy: Assign a skill only when the question or its explicit faithful adaptation requires the solver to perform that operation. Background, supplied results, available tools and grader metrics do not earn labels.

Use the most specific operation that describes the required result. Do not add generic statistics, regression, classification or data preparation for steps internal to a specialized operation unless a separate deliverable requires them.
Split skills when their inputs, scientific decisions or checkable outputs require different task designs. Algorithm names, file formats, organisms and packages remain context metadata.

Assign applications from the biological objects and endpoints actually analyzed. Clinical motivation, a cited publication, or an incidental gene name is insufficient. Leave unresolved applications empty.
A category frequency counts a requirement at most once per question record. Repeated studies and overlapping releases must be considered before using frequency to plan tasks.

Eligibility requires a faithful executable result contract. Pinning a method or reference can resolve ambiguity; a deterministic proxy alone does not validate a causal, clinical or experimental claim.
